name: WeLocale
author: sserghei

sections.description:
WeLocale translates your website into 50+ languages with one connection. No code changes, no
developer, live in minutes. Add your App Key and the WeLocale widget translates your site in
place, with a built-in language switcher and SEO hreflang tags (on paid plans).

  • One connection, no code changes
  • 50+ languages, AI-powered translations
  • Built-in language switcher
  • SEO hreflang tags (Pro and Scale plans)
  • Words are stored permanently and never reset monthly

You manage languages, translations, the switcher, and SEO in your WeLocale dashboard. This plugin
only connects your site using your App Key; translations are stored in your WeLocale account, not
in WordPress. The widget always loads its latest version from welocale.net, so improvements arrive
without updating this plugin.

External service

This plugin connects your site to WeLocale (https://welocale.net), a third-party website-translation
service, and requires a WeLocale account. When enabled, it loads the WeLocale widget script
(https://welocale.net/widget/latest/loader.js) on your public pages using your App Key. The widget
reads the visible text of your pages to translate it.

  • Terms of Service: https://welocale.net/terms
  • Privacy Policy: https://welocale.net/privacy
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. Create a free account at welocale.net.
  3. Add your website in the WeLocale dashboard and enter your domain (so your site is allowed).
  4. Open “Install snippet” and copy your Public app key (a UUID).
  5. In WordPress go to Settings → WeLocale, paste the Public app key, and save.
  6. Your site now shows the language switcher and can be translated. Manage languages, translations,
    the switcher, and SEO in your WeLocale dashboard.
sections.faq:
Do I need a WeLocale account?

Yes. A free plan is available at welocale.net. The plugin connects your site via your App Key.

Where do I manage translations?

In your WeLocale dashboard. The plugin only connects your site; it does not store translations.

Does it conflict with WPML or Polylang?

No. WeLocale translates the rendered front end at runtime and does not change how WordPress builds
your pages.
